findings.description: F002 has an ordering ambiguity: it says the removal-OUTCOME entry is appended after destructive steps finish, but later says only then does it run git worktree remove and delete the registry binding. That leaves the audit/removal/registry mutation sequence underdetermined.
findings.recommendation: Pin the exact sequence as preflight, durable removal-INTENT append, git worktree remove without force, registry binding delete, then removal-OUTCOME append with defined behavior for each failure point.

findings.description: F002 introduces a registry-only completion path after a prior audited intent, but the acceptance text only says it is itself audited. It does not pin whether that completion audit must be written before deleting the stale registry entry or how unwritable audit storage behaves on this path.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit acceptance and tests for registry-only completion: audit entry first, refuse if that audit write fails, then delete only the stale registry binding.

findings.description: F003 pins behavior when an allowlisted source file exists in repo_root, but it does not specify the source-absent matrix for environments.json. If the base checkout lacks the allowlisted file, create-time notices and --copy-local-config behavior could silently no-op.
findings.recommendation: Define and test source-absent cases explicitly: source absent and target absent, source absent and target present, and source absent with --copy-local-config.
